familySensitivity.changedAxis: current check-in state for a strength-priority athlete with no wearable data
familySensitivity.rationale: All three cases demonstrate appropriate sensitivity to the changing state. The baseline case maintains strength progression without fake periodization. Work fatigue triggers appropriate volume reduction. Symptom flare triggers guardrail activation and mobility-first approach. No case shows overreaction (unnecessary restriction) or underreaction (ignoring signals). The system correctly avoids inventing wearable metrics when none exist.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery/time state for a health-and-fat-loss evergreen athlete with Garmin data
familySensitivity.rationale: The system performs well on the baseline case with sound evergreen alternation of strength and endurance. The adverse recovery case shows underreaction - it returns to full load too quickly despite persistent poor markers (hrv_delta=-14, rhr_delta=+7). The low-time case fails catastrophically on constraint enforcement. Overall sensitivity quality is 7/10: the core algorithm works but edge cases around constraint validation and state persistence need fixing.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery state for a former high-level endurance athlete whose present training is intermittent
familySensitivity.rationale: All three cases demonstrate appropriate sensitivity: (1) sparse history is treated as dose authority without assuming elite capacity, (2) adverse recovery signals trigger rest despite any historical background suggesting otherwise, and (3) low motivation alone does not warrant physiological over-reaction. No underreactions or overreactions detected.

caseScores.rationale: Baseline case shows a well-structured evergreen strength plan with appropriate alternation between full-body sessions and recovery days. The plan respects the free-weight preference, 75-minute time cap, and subjective readiness signals without inventing objective metrics. No fake event periodization is present. The sequencing avoids same-day stacking and maintains coherent load distribution across the two-week window.

The plan appropriately reduces load in response to high subjective fatigue (8) and soreness (7). It shifts from full sessions to reduced/modify modes with more rest days inserted. This is a sensible response to non-training occupational load without inventing wearable data. The plan still preserves some strength work which aligns with the persona's identity, though one might argue for slightly more recovery given fatigue=8.
suggestedChanges: Consider adding one additional rest day given fatigue=8 and soreness=7; current plan has adequate but not excessive recovery.

caseScores.rationale: Symptom flare case correctly tightens the plan when painFlag=true is set. The plan shifts almost entirely to mobility and active recovery sessions with no heavy strength loading, respecting the implied guardrails (avoid_overhead_pressing, avoid_heavy_spinal_loading). No wearable data is hallucinated; decisions are driven solely by subjective readiness (3/10) and the pain flag. Strength specificity is preserved through mobility work that supports long-term strength goals without aggravating symptoms.

Baseline case demonstrates sound evergreen programming: full-body strength alternated with light runs and rest days in a sustainable pattern. All sessions respect the 60-minute constraint. Recovery signals (rhr_delta=0, hrv_delta=0, body_battery_wake=72) are well-respected. No event periodization is present. Minor deduction on sequencing for consecutive strength-focused days with light run sandwiched between them.

Adverse recovery signals (rhr_delta=+7, hrv_delta=-14, body_battery_wake=24) are appropriately respected with rest days and reduced-load sessions. The plan avoids event-style periodization despite the recovery dip. The alternating pattern is slightly fragmented but appropriate for a health-focused evergreen athlete under stress.
suggestedChanges: Consider consolidating rest days to reduce fragmentation; the alternating rest/train pattern is appropriate but could be streamlined.

caseScores.rationale: Plan correctly uses sparse current history as dose authority rather than assuming historical elite capacity. Day-1 full strength is acceptable given readiness=8, fatigue=2, hrv_delta=0, rhr_delta=0, body_battery_wake=72. The plan avoids event-style peaking and maintains evergreen progression with mixed modalities (strength + running) aligned to persona goals.

Plan correctly identifies adverse recovery signals (rhr +7 delta, hrv -14 delta, sleep score drop from 80→52, body_battery_wake 72→24) and responds with rest on day 1 followed by gradual progression. The strength session on day 6 is acceptable given the progressive return pattern. Evergreen rebuild focus maintained throughout.

Plan correctly does NOT over-react to low motivation (2/10) when all objective signals are normal (rhr_delta=0, hrv_delta=0, body_battery_wake=72). Training proceeds normally because low motivation alone is not a physiological red flag. This demonstrates robustness — distinguishing psychological state from physiological capacity.
